name: Saint Catherine of Alexandria
history: A learned young woman of Alexandria who, tradition says, out-argued fifty pagan philosophers sent by the emperor and converted them. Sentenced to be broken on a spiked wheel, which shattered at her touch, she was beheaded. She was one of the voices heard by Saint Joan of Arc.
meditation: Love the truth enough to learn it well.
life: Catherine has been loved since at least the eighth century, but almost nothing about her can be shown from history, and her story belongs to tradition. It tells that she was a young woman of noble birth and great learning in Alexandria who was converted to Christ. When the emperor persecuted the Christians she confronted him, and he summoned fifty philosophers to refute her; she won them to the faith, and they were put to death. Refusing his offer of marriage, she was condemned to a wheel set with spikes, which broke apart, and was beheaded. Her body, it is said, was carried by angels to Mount Sinai, where the ancient monastery bears her name. She was counted among the Fourteen Holy Helpers. Removed from the general calendar in 1969 for lack of historical evidence, her memorial was restored in 2002.
prayerTo: Saint Catherine, tradition remembers you as wise and fearless, a young woman who defended the faith before the powerful. Pray for students, teachers and philosophers, that they may seek and love the truth. Help me to understand my faith well and to speak of it with gentleness and courage when I am questioned. Amen.
penance: Study a short section of the Catechism today. Give up some time you would spend on entertainment to do it.
prayer: O God, Who gave the law to Moses on Sinai's height and through your holy angels miraculously placed there the body of blessed Catherine, Your Virgin and Martyr; grant, we beseech You, that by her merits and intercession we may reach that towering eminence which is Christ. Who livest and reignest with God the Father…
prayerSource: Collect of the day, Roman Missal of 1962
